_comment: Original writing for art.lore. {port} is replaced with a port name. Keep entries short: they are sent to the client one page at a time.

founding.title: The Charter
founding.text: Before the lanes had names, the islands traded by rowing boat and rumour. Then the tide-clerks of the old customs house wrote a single sheet listing every cargo, every hull and every port that would honour it. They called it the Manifest, and anyone who signed it could sail.

founding.title: The First Lane
founding.text: The first lane was a rope of buoys between two harbours that disliked each other. A grain skipper and a fuel skipper agreed to carry for both, for a fee, and found that the fee was larger than the grudge. Every lane since has been built on the same arithmetic.

founding.title: The Lamp Treaty
founding.text: Pirates burned three lighthouses in a single winter. The harbours answered with the Lamp Treaty: any port that keeps its lamp lit may fly the Manifest pennant and charge a docking fee. The patrol boats you see today are the treaty's teeth.

founding.title: The Season Clock
founding.text: To stop the richest houses owning the sea forever, the Charter resets every season. Ledgers are closed, fleets are counted, and a new map is chalked on the customs house wall. Old captains say the sea itself moves between seasons. New captains say the old ones drink.

founding.title: Your Signature
founding.text: Your name is the newest line on the Manifest. The clerks have already started a page for you. What goes on it is up to the weather, the market, and you.

biomes.name: palm reef
lines: {port} grew up around a reef that rings like glass when the tide turns. Divers swear the coral keeps time better than the harbour clock.
The palms of {port} lean seaward, and locals say they point toward the next good price.
Every dock post in {port} is painted a different colour, so drunk sailors can find their own boat by taste in colour alone.

biomes.name: green hills
lines: {port} is a town of hedges, chapels and very opinionated sheep. Its harbourmaster keeps a ledger of every ship that has ever been rude to him.
On a still morning the bells of {port} carry three islands over. Ferrymen use them as a fog signal and a reason to be late.
The quay at {port} was built from the stones of a castle nobody remembers owning.

biomes.name: pine coast
lines: {port} winters under snow for half the year. The pine smoke from its chimneys is said to cure seasickness, and certainly cures appetite.
In {port} the fishermen carve a small wooden gull for every friend lost at sea. The harbour wall is crowded with them.
Ice in the bay of {port} sings at night as it shifts. Children learn the songs before they learn to read.

biomes.name: red cliffs
lines: {port} sits under red cliffs that hold the day's heat long after dark. Traders eat late and argue later.
Water is dearer than fuel in {port}, and the townsfolk will tell you so before they tell you their names.
The wind at {port} carries sand far out to sea; sailors know they are close when their teeth start to crunch.

biomes.name: black sand
lines: {port} was built on black sand from a mountain that still grumbles. The market closes whenever the mountain clears its throat.
Hot springs bubble up between the warehouses of {port}. Dockers keep their tea warm by setting the pot on the ground.
Glass beads from the beaches of {port} once served as coin across the archipelago. Some captains still keep a pocketful for luck.

relics.name: A compass that points south
relics.text: Its needle swings stubbornly to the south. Whoever made it scratched 'home' on the lid.

relics.name: A ship's bell, cracked
relics.text: The bell of the Wandering Tern, which left with a cargo of clocks and was never logged again.

relics.name: A water-stained ledger
relics.text: Every page lists one cargo: forty crates of 'patience'. The buyer is never named.

relics.name: A treaty lamp
relics.text: One of the first lamps lit under the Lamp Treaty. It still smells faintly of whale oil and politics.

relics.name: A small figurehead
relics.text: A carved woman holding a ledger instead of a sword. Merchants rub her nose for luck.

relics.name: A chart with an extra island
relics.text: It shows an island that is on no other map. The coastline has been drawn, rubbed out, and drawn again.

relics.name: A glass-bead coin
relics.text: Black glass from a volcanic beach, threaded on cord. Once enough to buy a week of fuel.

relics.name: A bosun's whistle
relics.text: Blow it and every gull in earshot turns its head. They are not impressed.

relics.name: A faded pirate flag
relics.text: The skull has been patched with a grain sack. Even pirates economise.

relics.name: A dented teapot
relics.text: Engraved: 'Presented to the slowest freighter in the fleet, who always arrived'.

relics.name: A customs-house key
relics.text: Heavy brass. The customs house was rebuilt twice, and the key fits neither door.

relics.name: The last page of a logbook
relics.text: 'Day 56. Sold everything. Kept the ship. Would do it all again.'

bottles: A message in a bottle: 'If found, please tell my brother the ore price was not my fault.'
A message in a bottle: 'Day nine adrift. Have eaten all the grain. Have started on the cargo manifest.'
A message in a bottle: a child's drawing of a freighter, with far too many funnels.
A message in a bottle: 'The Lantern Queen passed us at midnight. No crew. Every lamp lit.'
A message in a bottle: 'Buy low, sell high, and never trust a gull.'
A message in a bottle: a recipe for fish stew that begins 'first, catch the fish'.
